solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quondam top pigeon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete name for a whipping top, the spinning toy
second meaning: a fancy breed of domestic pigeon with a hood-like crest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quondam' (former) marks the toy sense as obsolete; the pigeon is named for the veil-like feathers on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word both as an old term for a spinning toy and as a hooded breed of fancy pigeon.

clue.text: We're one up playing some states from the east

indicators.note: players move about freely, so these letters are put in play in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team winning a game against some eastern opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the former Eastern Bloc countries that joined the EU, contrasted with 'Old Europe'.

clue.text: Stupidly ruin a word for less mature?

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it without sense, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
per is the word that means 'a', as in 'ten pounds a day'

explanation.surface: Wondering whether ruining a word is a sign of immaturity.
explanation.definitionFit: Unripe is used of fruit or of people not yet fully developed, so the comparative means less grown-up.

clue.text: National broadcast for some Keralans

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A nationwide broadcast aimed at people in Kerala.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nair are a Hindu caste of Kerala in southern India, so they are some of its people.

clue.text: ____ in southeast are involved with cuts

definitions.text: ____ in southeast are involved with cuts

parts.note: the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: letters that are involved get tangled up together, so they come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank sentence about something in the southeast that has to do with cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank stands for the answer itself, so the whole sentence describes it: the tool sits 'in' the wordplay, which also describes what it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are pruning shears, a garden tool whose whole purpose is making cuts.

clue.text: Mephisto, eg, is natural when rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: nat. is the abbreviation for natural
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A wink at the puzzle's title: the devil gets up naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephistopheles is the devil of the Faust legend, and the puzzle series is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto is a devil figure, so he is an example of the Devil himself.

clue.text: I could feasibly make letter copy well?

definitions.text: I could feasibly make letter copy well?

indicators.note: feasibly suggests one possible way of putting things, so the letters are rearranged into one such form

parts.note: taken as written
er is a hesitant 'well'

explanation.surface: Someone musing that they might be able to copy letters well.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: such a person makes printing copies of type, letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrotyper makes electrotypes, metal duplicates of set type or plates made by electroplating, for printing.

clue.text: Single embracing friend? No, without anybody as it as was

indicators.note: one thing embracing another holds it inside
'No' contradicts the order just stated, so the friend does the holding, not the single

parts.note: an ally is a friend
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A lonely single asking whether to hug a friend, then deciding against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' turns round the embrace the surface states: it is the friend that holds the single. 'As was' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Alonely is an archaic form of alone, meaning by oneself with no company.

clue.text: Be diligent about appropriate apparent outing at work?

parts.note: to appropriate is to take
ap. is the abbreviation for apparent, as in heir apparent
a ride is an outing
someone at work is in

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a staff outing is the right sort of activity at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a pride in something is to care about it and do it conscientiously, an idiom for diligence.

clue.text: Sanction overturning misery that's in plea

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped over, so in a down entry its letters run upwards

parts.note: a bane is a cause of misery

indicators.note: what is in a word is its interior, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the inner two letters

explanation.surface: Approving an appeal by reversing someone's misery.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to authorise or permit, and to enable something is likewise to make it allowed or possible.

clue.text: Relative before being grubby

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an is an archaic conjunction meaning 'if', and dialect 'being' means 'since' or 'seeing that'

explanation.surface: A relative who was scruffy even before they arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means dirty or soiled, a near-synonym of grubby.

clue.text: Cunning owl leaving leisurely

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so the bird's letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: slowly means in a leisurely way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wily owl taking its time to depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leisurely' looks like it describes the owl's exit, but it is the word to be cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means crafty or underhand, a near-synonym of cunning.

clue.text: Sweet talk tart, foolish sort short on deceit

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: being short on something means lacking it, so the deceit is taken out of the foolish sort

parts.note: a nellie (or nelly) is a silly, soft person
a lie is a piece of deceit

explanation.surface: Someone charming a pastry-loving fool who is not very good at lying.
explanation.walkthrough: Nellie is old British slang for a silly person, familiar from the phrase 'not on your nellie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for smooth, flattering or evasive talk meant to win someone over.

clue.text: Store on disc legal document or the equivalent in return

parts.note: a writ is a written court order

indicators.note: something given in return comes back the other way, so these letters run from right to left

parts.note: o.t.e. is the abbreviation for 'or the equivalent', seen in job adverts

explanation.surface: Instructions for saving a legal document, or something like it, to a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To write data to a disc is to record or save it there, a computing idiom.

clue.text: Oh to hold centre-half in persistent pain

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so the exclamation goes round the footballer

parts.note: ay is an old interjection of grief or surprise, like 'ah!' or 'oh!'
the standard abbreviation for the football position

explanation.surface: A cry from a footballer playing centre-half who is nursing a lingering injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oh' looks like the speaker's groan, but it is the old interjection that holds the football position.
explanation.definitionFit: Achy describes a body suffering a dull, continuing soreness, the state of being in persistent pain.

clue.text: Right before food stuck into Scots supplement for chuckie?

indicators.note: something stuck into another thing is pushed inside it, so these letters go within the supplement

parts.note: eik is Scots for an addition or supplement
the usual abbreviation
a.c. is the prescription abbreviation for ante cibum, Latin for 'before food'

explanation.surface: A recipe note: put the right supplement into Scottish chicken feed before mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: RAC goes inside EIK, between the I and the K. 'Before food' looks like an order of events but is the pharmacist's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Scots words for a young hen; chuckie is a pet name for a chicken.

clue.text: The Devil is behind European law degree

indicators.note: being behind something means coming after it, so the verb-like word is placed last

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
BL is a Bachelor of Law
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that the Devil is behind the European degree in law, a lawyer joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is behind' places IS after the European law degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eblis (Iblis) is the chief evil spirit in Islamic tradition, equivalent to the Devil.

clue.text: Most heavy sod, it gets rotavated

indicators.note: rotavated soil is churned up by a machine, so these letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy clods of turf being broken up by a rotavator.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is heavy and filling, so the superlative is the heaviest and most indigestible.

clue.text: Work up lather and put one in a wide-awake state

indicators.note: working something up means stirring and mixing it, so these words are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wake-up routine: whip up shaving lather and get someone fully alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder: the letters of lather, put and one are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To be upon the alert is the older form of the idiom 'on the alert', meaning watchful and ready.

clue.text: Process of disengaging clapped out trailer

indicators.note: something clapped out is worn out and broken, so its letters are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unhitching a worn-out trailer from a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapped out is British slang for worn out from use.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiral is a chiefly Scottish word for retirement or withdrawing, a stepping back from active involvement.

clue.text: Biting rent in an open case full of sweet bits?

definitions.text: an open case full of sweet bits

parts.note: a tart remark is sharp and biting
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about the rent on an open legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open case' suggests a court matter or luggage, but it is a pastry shell with no lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a small open pastry case holding a sweet filling such as fruit or jam.

clue.text: Only just about accepted pressure in can

indicators.note: letters placed in something go inside it, here inside the slang word for the backside

parts.note: can and tush are both American slang for the buttocks
a. is a dictionary abbreviation for about
A marks an accepted bill of exchange
the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone barely managing to cram something into a tin under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is not a tin here; it is US slang for the bottom, as is TUSH. The first A stands at the front; the other two letters go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: At a push is a British idiom meaning with difficulty or if absolutely necessary, so only just.

clue.text: Hardship in western port when zone is closed off

indicators.note: something closed off is shut out of reach, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Penzance is a port in Cornwall, at Britain's western tip
z is the abbreviation for zone

explanation.surface: Suffering in a Cornish harbour town when a district is sealed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a harbour town at the far west of Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-inflicted suffering, so it can stand loosely for a hardship one must endure.

clue.text: Ferocious fish set up an absolute slaughter

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
A is an abbreviation for absolute
a rip is a violent tearing, a savaging

explanation.surface: A savage fish arranging a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string AN, A, RIP is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirana is a variant spelling of piranha, the South American freshwater fish with razor-sharp teeth.

clue.text: Previously bullied having wheels punctured by one

indicators.note: a thing punctured by something has that something poked inside it

parts.note: tyred means fitted with tyres
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A vehicle with wheels gets a puncture from a single nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks the definition as an obsolete form, which is fair in a puzzle that draws on Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrane is an obsolete verb meaning to tyrannise, so tyraned is an old word for oppressed or domineered.

clue.text: Backing one Rector up beat international chorus making moral

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the first three bits are read in reverse order

parts.note: the Roman numeral
the usual abbreviation
taken as written
to tan someone's hide is to beat them
the usual abbreviation
to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A cleric leading a rousing international choir that sings uplifting songs.
explanation.walkthrough: I, R and UP are reversed together to make PURI; the rest follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To puritanise is to make something puritan, imposing strict moral or religious standards on it.

clue.text: Rail is very much supported by port of entry

indicators.note: in a down entry, a thing supported by another sits on top of it, so the second piece goes underneath

parts.note: sore is an old adverb meaning greatly or very much

indicators.note: a port is where things come in, so the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A railway line that depends on a port of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The soree, or sora, is a small North American bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Those of an inferior sort body-swerving good old hostel

indicators.note: body-swerving is dodging round something, so that letter is avoided and left out

parts.note: gentry is used ironically for people of a contemptible kind, as in 'these gentry'
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Lowlifes dodging a respectable old hostel.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTRY sounds respectable, but is used here in its sneering sense; it loses its G. Body-swerve is a Scots word for dodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry once meant an inn or lodging house, the place one enters to stay, so it is an obsolete word for a hostel.

clue.text: Lord! A party returned Hislop, for example

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is written from right to left

parts.note: Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye; the name is reversed

explanation.surface: Exclaiming as Ian Hislop comes back to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is the editor of the British satirical magazine Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonai is a Hebrew name for God, meaning 'my Lord', and is used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Rob can bust with deuce!

explanation.walkthrough: Four meanings, not two: British slang for steal, for jail and for arrest, and the devil's nickname, since 'deuce' is a euphemism for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The one short word is slang for steal, a jail, an arrest, and (as Old Nick) the devil.

clue.text: Tincture or a material used by Lock & Co, et al

definitions.text: material used by Lock & Co, et al

parts.note: in heraldry, the gold tincture or was named sol, after the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of options for what a hatmaker might use: a dye, or some material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is not a conjunction: it is the heraldic gold. Lock & Co are London hatters, famous for tropical helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sola is the pith of an Indian plant used to make lightweight sun helmets, or topis, which hatters made.

clue.text: Dry secretary's party dumping it

parts.note: first meaning: of wine, not sweet
second meaning: the usual abbreviation

indicators.note: dumping something means throwing it away, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
the closing letter

explanation.surface: A dry secretary's party where nobody drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and a third route: SECT drops its T, the end of 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is French for dry, used of wine and champagne, and also an abbreviation of secretary.

clue.text: Sharing a parent's computer I network in limited scope

indicators.note: a limited scope means a narrow view, so only part of the phrase is looked at

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: Someone shares a parent's computer, with networking kept to a narrow range.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Uterine siblings are born of the same mother but different fathers, so they have one parent in common.

clue.text: Most calm prime of womenkind beside comfy home

parts.note: Eve was the first woman
a nest is a cosy home

explanation.surface: The finest woman at ease in her cosy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' here means first in order, not best.
explanation.definitionFit: Even can mean placid or unruffled, so the superlative is the most serene or level-tempered.

clue.text: Primate's reach ain't appointed

indicators.note: things appointed are arranged or fitted out, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church primate's power does not depend on being appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarhines are Old World monkeys and apes, a group of primates with close-set, downward nostrils.

clue.text: Flesher's dead meat is close to rank (and for les bouchers?)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter
et is French for 'and', the word French butchers would use

explanation.surface: A butcher's rotten meat nearly reeks, with a nod to French butchers.
explanation.walkthrough: Flesher is Scots for butcher, and les bouchers are French butchers, so 'and' in their language is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ket is a Scots and northern word for carrion, the rotten flesh of dead animals.
